cards.subject: The wandering
lines: Centuries of following the kodo herds with no fixed home, after losing the grassland that is now called Desolace.
They took this valley back from the centaur with orc help, and stopped.

cards.subject: The Rites of the Earthmother
lines: Strength, Vision, Wisdom. They are not a starter chain that ends at level six — they run from two to fourteen, from the mesa to Thunder Bluff.
Walking Mulgore is the rite.
All of it was deleted from the modern game. It exists only here now.

cards.subject: Arra'chea
cards.tag: The last rite is a hunt
lines: Cairne sends you to kill one specific kodo and bring back his horn.
Arra'chea does not stand in a camp. He walks a clockwise circuit of the entire valley, which is why people hunt for twenty minutes and decide he is dead.
The horn was once sought by Cairne himself. You are repeating something he did.

cards.subject: Baine, before he was anyone
lines: He hands you the Rite of Vision at level five and tells you to go and talk to the shaman.
Cairne's son, in a village of maybe fifteen buildings.
Everything he later becomes is not in this game yet. Stand next to him and he is an NPC with a yellow mark.

cards.subject: There are dwarves in Mulgore
lines: An Explorers' Guild excavation, running supply, in the tauren starting zone.
The village's answer at level eight is to send a teenager to interfere with it.
Most tauren players have no memory of dwarves being here at all.

cards.subject: Bloodhoof makes two things
cards.tag: A dozen tents on a lake
lines: This is the principal place wild kodo are tamed and sold. Every tauren riding one anywhere in the world got it here.
It is also known for its drums, which the wiki says are unlike any others.
A settlement this size supplies the Horde's mounts and its drums.

cards.subject: What the feathers are for
lines: The harpies in the far north drop out of the sky at you, and Thunder Bluff hunts them for their plumage.
The plumage is used at weddings and feasts.
The most hostile corner of the most peaceful zone exists so that people can decorate a wedding.

cards.subject: Wildmane Water Well
lines: The Venture Company seized it — not to mine it, to hold the water.
The tauren ran them off.
That is the whole northern half of this zone in one sentence: goblins reaching for the water, tauren pushing back.

cards.subject: The Ravaged Caravan
lines: A wrecked Venture Company camp on the shore, still smoking, still defended.
The tauren destroyed it and nobody cleaned it up.
It is the only place in Mulgore that looks like something bad happened, and it is on the prettiest lake in the zone.

cards.subject: One way out
lines: Mountains all the way round and a single pass east into the Barrens. No boat, no zeppelin, no dungeon, no second exit.
There is no flight master anywhere but Thunder Bluff. Everything else you walk, and the valley is flat and enormous.
It is the most peaceful zone in the game and the one people leave fastest, and those are the same fact.

cards.subject: Red Rocks
cards.tag: Where the tauren burn their dead
lines: Only the most valiant are laid to rest here.
Quilboar had moved in and fouled it, which is why the rite involves clearing them out.
Your coming of age finishes on the funeral ground.
